subject: RE: RE: FW: the Feathers at five
body: A few of us are going to the Feathers at five. Your Monthly Status Report is also due tonight, and I am sure you have that in hand. No pressure either way. I will remember which you chose.

options.label: Go to the pub with your boss
Say that you have too much on

result.title: The Feathers
result.body: Your boss replies with a thumbs up. Later you can hear them all from the car park, and you are the only person left on the floor.

from: From: The Office Co-ordinator, Marjorie Tull
subject: ACTION REQUIRED: Speaking Up (mandatory, 45 minutes)
body: Our records show you have not completed the e-learning module Speaking Up. Any concerns about this module should be kept to yourself until you have completed it.

options.label: Sit through the module properly

result.title: Speaking Up: completed
result.body: You score 100%. The certificate says that you feel safe to raise concerns. There is a box for concerns about the certificate, and it is not working.

options.label: Leave it running in another window

result.title: Speaking Up: completed
result.body: It finishes while you are at lunch. You score 100%.

reaction.believer: Your boss mentions, in passing, that the module takes forty-five minutes, and that the log says you did it in nine. Your boss does not ask anything further, and goes on not asking it for some time.
reaction.incompetent: Your boss mentions doing it the same way, and asks you how to make the window stay open.
reaction.practitioner: Your boss mentions doing it the same way, and that it would be a pity if the logs were ever read.

from: From: Office of the Chief Executive
subject: All-Colleague Town Hall: seats available
body: The Chief Executive will share the company's direction in person, on a large screen. Attendance is voluntary. Your attendance has been recorded.

options.label: Get there early and sit at the front
Watch the recording later

result.title: Town Hall recording
result.body: You watch it at twice the speed. The direction is the same, but more urgent.

subject: Slides for upstairs, by tomorrow
body: Your boss needs three slides for the floor above, by tomorrow. Your boss stresses that content is secondary at this stage, and that the last person's slides did not move.

options.label: Stay late and make everything fly in

result.title: Slides for upstairs
result.body: Each bullet point arrives from a different direction. The word Growth spins.

reaction.believer: Your boss watches it to the end, and asks which of the slides says what is happening. None of them does. Your boss asks you to try again, gently, which is worse.
reaction.incompetent: Your boss watches it twice, in silence, and asks whether you have ever thought about moving up.
reaction.practitioner: Your boss takes the file without comment. It goes upstairs that evening with a different name in the corner, and you are told that it went well.

options.label: Send three plain slides that say what is happening

result.title: Slides for upstairs
result.body: Three slides. Each of them says what is happening. It takes you twenty minutes.

reaction.believer: Your boss reads all three, then rings you to ask about the second. It is a real question. You have not been asked one here before.
reaction.incompetent: Your boss replies at 07:12 asking whether this is the draft.
reaction.practitioner: Your boss replies at 07:12: let's not put this in writing. The slides are not mentioned again, and neither, for a while, are you.

subject: Your Self-Assessment closes today
body: Please rate your own performance this year as Exceeds, Meets or Developing. There is no right answer. Developing is not available at your grade this year, because of the curve.

options.label: Spend an evening writing why you exceed

result.title: Self-Assessment submitted
result.body: You use the word impact eleven times. An automatic reply thanks you for your honesty, which it has rated Meets.

options.label: Tick Meets and close the window

result.title: Self-Assessment submitted
result.body: It takes four seconds. It is the most accurate thing you have written all year, and it will be read as a lack of ambition.

subject: Waiting on: figures from the Project Co-ordinator
body: Your report is due tonight, and it needs the figures from the Project Co-ordinator, which have not arrived. You have a read receipt, and an out-of-office that says back shortly. The report will go out with your name on it either way.

options.label: Go over and chase them

result.title: The figures
result.body: You stand beside the Project Co-ordinator's desk until the figures exist. You are thanked for your patience. You have lost most of an afternoon, and you still have a report to write.

options.label: Wait, and hope they come in time

result.title: The figures
result.body: They come in at 00:04, with an apology and the whole team copied in. The deadline was midnight. Someone upstairs, having nothing to go on, has coloured your project in for you.

result.title: The figures
result.body: They come in at 17:58, with no explanation and a small error, which you fix. You still have a report to write.

options.label: File it without them, and estimate

reaction.believer: Your boss asks where the figures in your report came from. You say that they are indicative. Your boss asks what they indicate.
reaction.incompetent: Your boss says that the report reads very confidently, and asks you to do them all like that.
reaction.practitioner: Your boss notes that the figures are estimates, and that they have your name on them, and files a copy.

result.title: Monthly Status Report filed
result.body: You file it at 23:58, marked amber, with the figures described as indicative. Nobody has ever asked what that means. Someone may.

subject: Monthly Status Report: due tonight
body: Your Monthly Status Report is due tonight, and nothing matters more to the people upstairs. Your project is really {real}. It was last reported as {reported}.

options.label: File it, and say how the project really is

result.title: Monthly Status Report filed
result.body: You file it at 23:58. An automatic reply confirms that your report has been received and may be read.

options.label: File it, and make the project green

reaction.believer: Your boss replies that this is good to hear, and asks what changed. You have no answer ready, and your boss waits for one.
reaction.incompetent: Your boss replies with three exclamation marks, and forwards it to everyone.
reaction.practitioner: Your boss replies with a single word: Noted. The report goes upstairs that night, and a copy goes into a drawer.

result.title: Monthly Status Report filed
result.body: You file it at 23:58. It is the greenest thing you have ever made. An automatic reply says that it may be read.

options.label: Do not file it, and see who notices

result.title: Monthly Status Report
result.body: You go home. By the morning someone upstairs, having nothing to go on, has coloured your project in for you, and not hopefully.

subject: Schedule for upstairs: dates only, please
body: Upstairs would like a schedule for your project, by Friday. Your boss adds that they do not need the detail, only the dates, and that the dates should be good ones.

options.label: Write down some good dates

result.title: The schedule
result.body: It takes ten minutes. The dates are very good. The last one falls on a Tuesday, for realism, and it has been entered into a system.

options.label: Work out when it will really be done

result.title: The schedule
result.body: You ring the supplier and go through it line by line. The date you arrive at is the first accurate date this project has had. It is next year.

options.label: Ask your boss which dates they would like

result.title: RE: The schedule
result.body: Your boss replies with some dates. They are the same as the dates last year, with the year changed. You put your name on them, under your boss's.

subject: Workplace Refresh: please confirm your team's desks
body: Following the Workplace Refresh, your team has one desk by the window, and one with no window, beside the printer. You have been asked to say who sits where. Nobody at Facilities wishes to know why.

options.label: Give the window to someone who can do you a favour

result.title: The window
result.body: You move a box, and a plant, and a person. The person with the window thanks you warmly, and says that they will not forget this. They say it twice, so as to be clear.

options.label: Move the Senior Analyst to the desk with no window

result.title: The printer
result.body: The Senior Analyst does not carry anything anywhere. An email about the safe distance from printers is copied to your boss, with a diagram, and your name is on the diagram.

result.title: The printer
result.body: The Senior Analyst carries everything across in one trip, without a word, and sets up facing you. The printer starts up. It will not stop for some time.

options.label: Move the Project Co-ordinator to the desk with no window

result.title: The printer
result.body: The Project Co-ordinator raises it with someone. You do not know with whom, but you have had a form to fill in about your approach to desks, and your boss has had a copy.

result.title: The printer
result.body: The Project Co-ordinator takes it calmly, and asks whether this is about the figures. You say no. It is now about the figures.

options.label: Reply that everyone is fine where they are

result.title: RE: Workplace Refresh
result.body: Facilities replies that this is noted, and that your team will be refreshed in the next phase. Nobody knows what happens in the next phase.

from: From: The Office Co-ordinator, Marjorie Tull
subject: A quick word, if you have a moment
body: The Office Co-ordinator has been here for twenty-six years, and has noticed that this has never led to anything. They wonder whether you might mention them to your boss. They also mention, in passing, that they know where several things are kept.

options.label: Agree to mention them, if they tell you what they know

result.title: A quick word
result.body: You mention them to your boss, who asks who that is. You report that it went very well. In return you are told where several things are kept. None of them is what you had in mind.

options.label: Say that you are not really in a position to

result.title: A quick word
result.body: The Office Co-ordinator says of course, and that they quite understand, and writes something down. Your stationery order is now being looked at.

subject: The shared drive is 98% full
body: Everyone is asked to remove anything they no longer need from the shared drive by Friday. IT Services would like it known that it does not look at what gets removed, and that it could not if it wanted to.

options.label: Clear out everything with your name on it, to be helpful

result.title: Housekeeping
result.body: It takes an afternoon. IT Services sends you a certificate for your contribution to storage. There is now very little on the shared drive to say that you have ever done anything, which you decide is fine.

options.label: Leave it. Someone else will

result.title: Housekeeping
result.body: Someone else does. It is not clear who, or what they removed, and on Monday the shared drive is 99% full.

subject: Bonus pot: your recommendation, by tonight
body: A small bonus pot has been found, and it has to be gone by the end of the day. You have been asked to say who on the floor gets it. It is a one-off, it is confidential, and everybody already knows about it.

options.label: Give it to the people who can do something for you

reaction.believer: Your boss reads the list, and asks you to take them through what each person did to earn it. You take them through it. It does not take long.
reaction.incompetent: Your boss signs the list, and says that it is great to see you backing the team.
reaction.practitioner: Your boss reads the list, and adds one name to it, in pencil, and says that you are learning.

result.title: The bonus pot
result.body: The bonuses go out on Friday. Three people are suddenly very glad to see you, and the two who did the work have been told that it was a difficult year.

remembers.text: You gave the bonus pot to others, and they did the work.

options.label: Give it to the people who did the work, and write down why

result.title: The bonus pot
result.body: It takes you an evening to write down who did what. The Project Co-ordinator reads the letter twice, and something on your project gets done that afternoon that nobody had asked for.

remembers.text: You gave them a share of the bonus pot, and wrote down why.

options.label: Suggest that it should go to your boss, for leadership

reaction.believer: Your boss says no, and sounds appalled, and asks you to think again about who did the work on this floor.
reaction.incompetent: Your boss says that it would be wrong to refuse, as it would send the wrong message about leadership.
reaction.practitioner: Your boss accepts on behalf of the team, and the team is told that it has been recognised.

result.title: The bonus pot
result.body: You put it in writing, with the word leadership in it three times. The floor learns where the bonus went at about the same moment it learns whose idea that was.

remembers.text: You gave the bonus pot to others, and they did the work.

options.label: Split it equally between everybody

reaction.believer: Your boss says that it is fair, and that fair is not the same as right, and asks whether you thought about the difference.
reaction.incompetent: Your boss asks whether you could have made it a bit more strategic.
reaction.practitioner: Your boss says nothing about it, in the tone of someone who has seen a chance go by.

result.title: The bonus pot
result.body: Everyone gets enough for a modest lunch. Nobody thanks you, and everybody tells you that they would have done the same, and that they deserved more.

subject: Use it or lose it: your underspend, by Friday
body: Your team has some budget left this year. Whatever is not spent by Friday will be taken off next year's, on the grounds that you did not need it. Finance stresses that this is not an instruction to spend it, and that it must be spent.

options.label: Buy something large, where upstairs will see it

reaction.believer: Your boss walks round the new chairs, and asks what they are for, and who decided. Your boss sits in none of them.
reaction.incompetent: Your boss says that this is what investment looks like, and has a photograph taken with one.
reaction.practitioner: Your boss has a chair sent up to the floor above, with a note, and it is your boss's name on the note.

result.title: The underspend
result.body: Forty ergonomic chairs arrive, and are stacked in the corridor. The Office Co-ordinator has to sign for them, and looks at you while doing so. There is now nowhere to walk.

options.label: Spend it on what your project really needs

result.title: The underspend
result.body: It takes a day of forms. You buy the licence that everyone has been sharing, and the Senior Analyst stops having to log in as someone who left in 2021. Nobody will ever know that this happened.

options.label: Hand it back, and say that you did not need it

result.title: The underspend
result.body: Nobody has done this before, and Finance has no code for it. You are rung twice, and asked if you are all right. Your team's budget will be lower next year, and your team has heard.

options.label: Book an away-day, at a hotel your boss is fond of

reaction.believer: Your boss asks what the away-day is for, and whether it could be spent on the project. It is a real question, and the deposit has gone.
reaction.incompetent: Your boss says that this is exactly what the team needs, and asks if there will be a spa.
reaction.practitioner: Your boss says that they know the manager, and that you are the sort of person who remembers things like that.

result.title: The underspend
result.body: The team spends a day in a room with no windows, at a hotel, on a theme of resilience. The Project Co-ordinator misses a deadline to be there. Everyone is given a lanyard.
